newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary grains futures rise across the board.
newsitem.headline: Hungary grains futures rise across the board.

text.p: The grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange closed the week with an across-the-board rise on Friday and traders said the rise is set to continue.
"International prices are rising, but otherwise no fundamentals explain this upward trend," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
Milling wheat futures rose by the daily allowed 400 forints limit for all maturities, closing at 25,500 forints per tonne for May and 23,400 forints for December.
Arbitrage deals between Hungarian and west European markets also contributed to the rise, Herczeg said.
"There are many open selling positions in west Europe with the intention to cover them by purchases from our region," he said.
The general price increase could push maize higher as well, but Herczeg said sharp rises are not likely.
"Romania and Serbia are also selling maize, export outlooks remain poor," he said.
Maize prices rose for all but the December maturity, which remained unchanged at 19,200 forints. Other maturities ended between 18,300 forints for May and 18,850 forints for November.
Feed barley prices rose by limit for July, August and September but Herczeg said that similarly to maize, feed barley could not rise much further.
He also added that he expects prices to tumble in the longer term led by a drop in wheat prices due to expectations of a good crop.
"The planted are is large, the weather is good, everything points to a good crop," he said. "Too much or too little rain could cause some problems, but not before May".
